claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're asking about, and if so, how many children are you responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 15 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask you a few questions to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex? For example, do you live with him and/or pay for his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives with me and I pay for everything - his food, clothes, school things, all his needs really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very helpful. A few more questions:

**Is Alex currently in any approved education or training (such as school or college)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's at school, yes. Just doing his GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

1. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

2. **Is Alex in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. And no, he's not in hospital or care - he lives at home with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all - he's focused on his schoolwork. And he doesn't get any benefits in his own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the requirements:

✓ You live in the UK
✓ You are responsible for Alex - he lives with you and you provide for all his needs
✓ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
✓ Alex is in approved education (school, studying for GCSEs)
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
✓ Alex lives at home full-time (not in hospital or care)
✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week or receiving benefits in his own right

You can proceed with claiming Child Benefit for Alex. If you haven't already claimed, you can do so through the government's Child Benefit application process.

**Important note:** When Alex turns 16, you can continue to receive Child Benefit as long as he stays in approved education or training until he's under 20. Just make sure to keep HMRC updated about his education status.

Also, be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
